Up to 75% of its total expected cash outflows

Applying RBI's minimum haircuts and the 15% (Level 2B) and 40% (Level 2) caps, what is its stock of HQLA (approximately)?

options.text: ₹666.7 crore
₹720.0 crore
₹670.0 crore
₹900.0 crore

solution.concept: Stock of HQLA with haircuts and caps
solution.explanation: Adjusted Level 2A = 85% × 200 = 170; adjusted Level 2B = 50% × 300 = 150. Stock of HQLA = 400 + 170 + 150 − 50 − 3.3 ≈ ₹666.7 crore. Check: Level 2 is then exactly 40% and Level 2B exactly 15% of the stock.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹720 crore ignores both caps; ₹670 crore applies only the 15% cap; ₹900 crore ignores haircuts and caps.
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹666.7 crore

fact_checks.claim: Stock of HQLA = Level 1 + Level 2A + Level 2B - Adjustment for 15 per cent cap - Adjustment for 40 per cent cap; Adjustment for 15 per cent cap = Max [{Adjusted Level 2B - 15/85 * (Adjusted Level 1 + Adjusted Level 2A)}, {Adjusted Level 2B - 15/60 * Adjusted Level 1}, 0]; Adjustment for 40 per cent cap = Max {(Adjusted Level 2A + Adjusted Level 2B - Adjustment for 15 per cent cap) - 2/3 * (Adjusted Level 1 assets), 0}

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Ritu complained to her bank on 1 September 2026. The bank rejected her complaint by a reply dated 12 September 2026, and she is not satisfied. Under RB-IOS, 2026, when can she approach the RBI Ombudsman?

options.text: Only after 30 days from her complaint, i.e. from 1 October 2026, and by 30 December 2026
Only after 30 days from her complaint, and by 11 December 2026
Immediately, and by 12 March 2027 (six months from the reply)
Immediately, and no later than 90 days from the bank's reply, i.e. by 11 December 2026

solution.concept: When a complaint can be filed
solution.explanation: The 30-day wait applies only when the regulated entity has not replied. A complainant who has received a reply and is dissatisfied may approach the Ombudsman at once. The complaint must be made within 90 days from the expiry of the reply period or from the RE's last communication, whichever is later; here the last communication is 12 September, so the limit is 12 September + 90 days = 11 December 2026.
steps: Reply received and not satisfied → no need to wait 30 days
solution.why_others_wrong: Waiting 30 days is needed only when there is no reply; six months is not the limit.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Immediately, and no later than 90 days from the bank's reply, i.e. by 11 December 2026

fact_checks.claim: A complaint can be filed before the RBI Ombudsman if the complainant has not received any reply within 30 days ... or if the complainant is not satisfied with the reply/resolution provided by the Regulated Entity. Both the complainant and the regulated entity must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard, orally or in writing
The Appellate Authority must approve the draft Award
The regulated entity's Board must consent to the Award

solution.why_others_wrong: There is no deposit, no prior approval by the Appellate Authority and no Board consent requirement.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both the complainant and the regulated entity must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard, orally or in writing

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Customers file complaints against four NBFCs registered with RBI, none of them an excluded type (figures as per the audited balance sheet of the previous year):
P. A deposit-taking NBFC with assets of ₹60 crore.
Q. A non-deposit-taking NBFC with customer interface and assets of ₹150 crore.
R. A deposit-taking NBFC with assets of ₹20 crore.
S. A non-deposit-taking NBFC with customer interface and assets of ₹90 crore.
Against which of them can a complaint be filed under RB-IOS, 2026?

options.text: P and Q only
Q only
P, Q, R and S
P, Q and R only

solution.explanation: RB-IOS, 2026 covers NBFCs (other than the excluded types) that either are authorised to accept deposits or have customer interface with assets of ₹100 crore and above. The ₹100 crore threshold applies only to the customer-interface limb, so every deposit-taking NBFC (P and R) is covered whatever its size; Q (₹150 crore) is covered; S (₹90 crore, non-deposit) is not.
steps: Deposit-taking → covered regardless of size (P, R)
Customer interface → needs ≥ ₹100 crore (Q yes, S no)
solution.why_others_wrong: 'P and Q only' wrongly applies the ₹100 crore test to deposit-taking R; 'Q only' does the same to P and R; S is below the threshold.
solution.final_answer: Option D: P, Q and R only

options.text: A borrower's complaint that the bank has not returned his title deeds after he closed his home loan
An IT vendor's dispute with a bank over unpaid software licence fees
A bank officer's grievance that he was denied promotion
A customer's grievance against the personal conduct of a bank's executive director

solution.explanation: RB-IOS, 2026 deals with deficiency in service to customers. Disputes between a vendor and a regulated entity, disputes involving the employee-employer relationship, and grievances against the management or executives of the RE are expressly non-maintainable. Failure to return property documents after loan closure is a deficiency in service to a customer.
solution.why_others_wrong: The vendor, employee and management grievances fall under the excluded categories.
solution.final_answer: Option A: A borrower's complaint that the bank has not returned his title deeds after he closed his home loan

fact_checks.claim: Disputes between a vendor and a Regulated Entity. Grievances against Management or Executives of a Regulated Entity ... Disputes involving employee-employer relationship of a Regulated Entity

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025, besides the Information Technology Act, 2000, which data-protection law must banks continuously adhere to in their digital banking operations?

options.text: The Right to Information Act, 2005
The Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 only

solution.explanation: The general guidelines require banks offering digital banking to adhere continuously to the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and other legal requirements, with legal jurisdiction within India, along with FEMA, KYC/AML and DPSS instructions.
steps: Digital banking → IT Act, 2000 + DPDP Act, 2023
solution.why_others_wrong: The RTI Act and CICRA are not the data-protection law named; the PSS Act is relevant but is not a data-protection law.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank offers only a 'view only' digital banking facility. Under RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, which of the following can it offer through this facility?

options.text: Downloadable application forms for a loan
A personal loan sanctioned and disbursed online
An IMPS transfer to another bank
A bill payment from the savings account

solution.explanation: A view-only facility allows only services that do not alter the customer's assets or liabilities, such as balance enquiry, balance viewing and statement download. Loans, fund transfers and other facilities that create a liability or move funds cannot be provided, though downloadable forms for them can.
steps: View only → no change in assets/liabilities
Loans, transfers, payments → transactional facility needed
solution.why_others_wrong: Loans, IMPS transfers and bill payments move funds or create liabilities, so they need a transactional facility.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Downloadable application forms for a loan

fact_checks.claim: View Only Banking Facility – A feature of digital banking channels which only allows banking services that do not alter the asset or liability of the customer viz. balance enquiry, balance viewing, account statement download, etc. Note: Loans, funds transfers, and other such facilities ... cannot be provided by banks having view only facility over digital channels. However, banks providing view only facility can provide downloadable forms for such facilities

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, what must a bank ensure when it offers mobile banking through USSD or SMS rather than a mobile app?

options.text: The service must be limited to customers of a single partner telecom operator
The service must be restricted to balance enquiry only
The service must be offered only to customers with smartphones
The service must be network independent, usable by customers of all mobile network operators

solution.explanation: The Directions define mobile banking to include mobile applications, USSD and SMS. A bank offering mobile banking other than through apps must ensure that customers across mobile network operators can use it, i.e. the service must be network independent.
solution.why_others_wrong: Tying the service to one operator, to balance enquiry or to smartphones contradicts the rule and the purpose of USSD/SMS banking.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The service must be network independent, usable by customers of all mobile network operators

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: When a bank releases a new version of its mobile banking app, RBI's Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026 require it to deactivate older versions within what time?

options.text: Within 30 days of the release of the newer version
Within one year of the release of the newer version
Only when customers voluntarily update the app
In a phased, time-bound manner not exceeding six months from the release of the newer version

solution.explanation: Banks must deactivate older application versions in a phased but time-bound manner, not exceeding six months from the date of release of a newer version, so that only one version (apart from the overlap period) is maintained on each platform.
steps: New version released → old one deactivated within 6 months
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 days and one year are not the prescribed limit, and leaving it to customers defeats the control.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026, when must a bank's mobile application require the user to re-authenticate?

options.text: Each time the user launches the app, and whenever the device or app remains unused for a designated period
Only once, at the time of first registration on the device
Only for transactions above ₹10,000
Only when the user changes the mobile handset

solution.explanation: The mobile application shall require re-authentication whenever the device or application remains unused for a designated period and each time the user launches it. It must also not store passwords or keys on the device and must wipe sensitive data from memory when the user exits.
solution.why_others_wrong: One-time authentication, amount thresholds or handset change alone do not meet the requirement.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Each time the user launches the app, and whenever the device or app remains unused for a designated period

I. The bank's 'Gap Assessment and Internal Controls Adequacy' (GAICA) report must be certified by CERT-In empanelled third-party auditor(s).
II. The bank must meet the minimum paid-up capital or net worth under its licensing requirement as on 31 March of the immediately preceding financial year.
III. A bank that has implemented Core Banking Solution is exempt from the minimum CRAR requirement for this purpose.
Which of the above is/are correct?

I and III only
I and II only

The paid-up capital/net worth is tested as on 31 March of the immediately preceding financial year. CBS does not exempt a bank from the CRAR condition.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Authentication Directions, 2025 require at least two factors of authentication for digital payments, with listed exemptions. Which of the following card transactions still requires two-factor authentication?

options.text: The third monthly debit under an e-mandate already registered on a credit card
The first transaction under a new recurring e-mandate on a credit card
A payment made from a gift PPI
A small-value contactless card payment at a shop

First e-mandate transaction → needs two factors
Gift PPIs and small-value contactless → exempt

Tokenised issuance and settlement of corporate bonds

The amount is credited to a suspense account of Nepal SBI Ltd until claimed
The amount is converted into a fixed deposit in the beneficiary's name
The remittance is forfeited and transferred to a depositor education fund

Only a civil suit, since RTGS payments are final and irrevocable
A complaint to NPCI's dispute resolution system

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), RTGS handled 20 crore transactions worth ₹1,246 lakh crore in CY 2021 and 33 crore transactions worth ₹2,206 lakh crore in CY 2025. Which statement is correct?

The average transaction rose from about ₹6.2 lakh to about ₹6.7 lakh
Value grew faster than volume, so the average RTGS transaction rose from about ₹62 lakh to about ₹67 lakh
The average transaction stayed unchanged at about ₹65 lakh

solution.explanation: Average size = value ÷ volume. CY 2021: ₹1,246 lakh crore ÷ 20 crore = ₹62.3 lakh; CY 2025: ₹2,206 lakh crore ÷ 33 crore ≈ ₹66.8 lakh. RBI reports CAGRs of 13.5% in volume and 15.3% in value, consistent with a rising average.
solution.why_others_wrong: The average rose, not fell; ₹6.2–6.7 lakh is off by a factor of ten; it did not stay unchanged.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Value grew faster than volume, so the average RTGS transaction rose from about ₹62 lakh to about ₹67 lakh

No; only failures caused by technical faults such as link failures are covered
No; any failure involving the customer's own input is excluded altogether
Only if the amount exceeds ₹2 lakh

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank's required CRR for the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026 is ₹10,000 crore. Its daily CRR balances are ₹10,150 crore, ₹9,950 crore, ₹9,880 crore and ₹10,100 crore on the first four days and ₹10,000 crore on each of the other ten days. Which statement is correct under RBI's circular of 9 October 2026?

options.text: The fortnightly average (about ₹10,006 crore) is adequate, but the ₹9,880 crore day breaches the daily floor of ₹9,900 crore
The bank complies fully, since the daily floor is ₹9,000 crore
The bank fails because its balance fell below ₹10,000 crore on two days
The bank fails because the fortnightly average is below ₹10,000 crore

solution.explanation: The average must be at least the required CRR, and every day's balance at least 99% of it. Average = (10,150 + 9,950 + 9,880 + 10,100 + 10 × 10,000) ÷ 14 ≈ ₹10,006 crore, which is adequate. Daily floor = 0.99 × 10,000 = ₹9,900 crore; the ₹9,880 crore day falls short, while ₹9,950 crore is within the floor.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹9,000 crore was the floor under the old 90% rule; balances between 99% and 100% on a day are allowed; the average is above the requirement.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The fortnightly average (about ₹10,006 crore) is adequate, but the ₹9,880 crore day breaches the daily floor of ₹9,900 crore
